app/src/pages/ability.ts — feature is a single self-contained file
app/src/pages/pokemon.ts:118-127 — Abilities section inlined in another page's HTML string, must be edited separately
app/index.html:14-16 — nav has no Abilities link, nothing to clean up there
removability.rationale: Deleting a feature means deleting its page file, its router branch, and one embedded section in the Pokémon page — no dead links, no orphan CSS, but the feature isn't fully self-contained because a slice of it lives inside another page.

evidence: app/src/components.ts:28 — every card list renders via pokemonCard, so a sprite fix is one call site
app/src/pages/ability.ts:20-33 — duplicates the species-mapping logic of data.ts:96-110, so a mapping fix lands twice
app/src/pages/pokemon.ts:276-292 — table sort data re-parsed from rendered DOM textContent, so display changes can silently break sorting
changeability.rationale: Most cross-cutting behavior (sprites, escaping, names, not-found detection) funnels through single helpers, so the typical bug fix is one obvious place. Two duplicated re-implementations (ability's species mapping, the DOM-reparse sorter) are the exceptions.

evidence: app/src/api.ts — fetch, base URL, and cache are isolated behind apiJson/spriteUrl
app/src/data.ts — all derived maps behind memoized getters with narrow return types
app/src/nav.ts:9-12 — tiny nav bus; pages don't import the router
app/server.mjs — server concerns fully separated from src/
app/src/pages/home.ts:135 — bypasses nav.ts and calls history.pushState directly, so URL-update knowledge lives in two places
coupling.rationale: Modules depend on narrow, well-documented interfaces and there's a real server/client seam. Minor tangles: the view layer imports spriteUrl from the API module, home bypasses the nav bus, and the type-name-resolution idiom (typeNames.get(x) ?? humanize(x)) is repeated in three pages.

evidence: app/src/components.ts:23-45 — pokemonCard/cardList/typeBadge stretch across four pages via options, not flags
app/src/data.ts:96-110 — speciesFromPokemonRefs serves three pages but didn't stretch to ability's hidden-ability case
app/src/pages/pokemon.ts:133-254 — moves section is a 120-line monolith mixing fetch, grouping, HTML building and wiring
app/src/pages/move.ts:9-15 — the fetch/404/title scaffold is hand-copied in every resource page instead of a shared helper
abstraction_design.rationale: The card/section/data abstractions are genuinely shaped around the app's real variation and get reused everywhere, but two seams failed when variation appeared (ability copied rather than extended the species mapper; no page scaffold means each new resource type starts as a copy), and the moves section would grow flag-shaped under further change.

findings.issue: Re-implements speciesFromPokemonRefs (data.ts:96-110) inline to also capture the hidden flag; fixes to species-mapping rules (dedup, ordering, name fallback) must be made twice.
findings.suggestion: Extend speciesFromPokemonRefs to return the full ref plus optional metadata (e.g. an options argument or a richer return shape) and have ability.ts consume it.

findings.issue: Sortable move data is reconstructed by parsing rendered cells' textContent and scraping hrefs; any change to how values are displayed (or the '—' sentinel) silently corrupts sorting.
findings.suggestion: Keep the MoveRow[] objects in scope and pass them to wireMovesSection (or stash as a data attribute), sorting the model and re-rendering rather than round-tripping through the DOM.

findings.issue: The /api/v2/ path prefix is baked into toUrl alongside the base URL, so 'change the data source' touches string assembly in two spots within the same file.
findings.suggestion: Treat the full endpoint prefix (base + /api/v2) as one configured value, or accept API paths already including /api/v2.

findings.issue: The default base URL 'http://localhost:9000' is duplicated in api.ts:7, server.mjs:14 and vite.config.ts:16; changing the default means three edits that can drift.
findings.suggestion: Centralize the default in one shared constant/config module imported by server.mjs and vite.config.ts (the browser bundle only needs the injected value).

findings.issue: Calls history.pushState/replaceState directly instead of the nav.ts navigate() bus, so URL mutation knowledge exists in two modules.
findings.suggestion: Add a navigate(url, {replace, render:false}) capability to nav.ts and use it here, or document that home deliberately re-renders locally.

findings.issue: The fetch → isNotFound → renderNotFound → title pattern is copy-pasted in move.ts, ability.ts, types.ts and pokemon.ts; a new resource page (e.g. Items) must copy it again.
findings.suggestion: Extract a withResource(root, path, render) helper that owns 404 handling and the document.title convention.

findings.issue: Module-level sectionCounter is hidden mutable global state used to uniquify heading ids; ids grow across renders and the coupling to aria-labelledby is implicit.
findings.suggestion: Derive the id from the section title (as already done) without a counter, or pass ids explicitly from callers that need stable anchors (like the moves section already does).

summary: A small, well-seamed vanilla TS app where pages are independent files, cross-cutting concerns funnel through single helpers (spriteUrl, pokemonCard, util, api cache), and server/client code is cleanly separated. Its main editability debts are two duplicated re-implementations (ability's inline species mapping, the moves table's DOM-reparse sorter) and the absence of a shared page scaffold, which makes adding a new resource type a copy-paste exercise. Most requested changes land in one to four obvious, greppable places.
